mainTopic: Oils on יום טוב, and mentioning חנוכה and ראש חודש in ברכת המזון and מוסף
overview: This amud opens with a ברייתא that supports רב חסדא: oils that may not be used for שבת lights may be used on יום טוב, except שמן שריפה. The גמרא then asks whether חנוכה is mentioned in ברכת המזון. The answer is that it is not required, but whoever mentions it puts it in the הודאה blessing, just as in תפילה. Next it asks the same question about ראש חודש, and רב and רבי חנינא disagree. רב זריקא rules like רב, based on a ברייתא of רבי אושעיא. That ברייתא teaches that days with a קרבן מוסף are mentioned in ברכת המזון, while fast days without one are not. Finally, the גמרא asks whether חנוכה is mentioned in מוסף, and two pairs of אמוראים disagree. אביי tries to link the 'no mention' view to a ruling of רב about the הפטרה on שבת ראש חודש. The גמרא rejects that comparison and finds a better one in רב's ruling about the מנחה הפטרה on a יום טוב that falls on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא about oils on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches רב חסדא's view. Oils that are forbidden for שבת lights are allowed on יום טוב, except שמן שריפה, because קדשים may not be burned on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with רב חסדא: all the oils that the Sages said may not be lit on שבת may be lit on יום טוב. The one exception is שמן שריפה (impure תרומה oil that must be burned), because consecrated items may not be burned on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב חסדא said earlier. This backs up his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, many oils are banned for lighting because of concerns like the flame burning poorly, which could lead someone to tilt the lamp. Those concerns do not apply on יום טוב, so the oils are allowed. שמן שריפה is still forbidden for a different reason: burning קדשים is a מצוה that may not be done on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him; a supporting source
Impure תרומה oil that must be burned

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, all the oils banned on שבת may be lit except שמן שריפה, because קדשים may not be burned on יום טוב.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Chisda.
All of these oils about which the Sages said
one may not light with them on Shabbat,
one may light with them on a Festival,
except for burnt oil (impure terumah oil)

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין שׂוֹרְפִין קׇדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: because one may not burn consecrated items on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion of רב חסדא's ruling by supplying a ברייתא that supports it.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that oils forbidden for שבת lights are permitted on יום טוב, except שמן שריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the identical rule and its reason

steps.title: Must חנוכה be mentioned in ברכת המזון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether חנוכה is mentioned in ברכת המזון. One side says no, since it is only דרבנן. The other side says yes, because of פרסומי ניסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the rule about mentioning חנוכה in ברכת המזון? Since חנוכה is only rabbinic, maybe we do not mention it. Or perhaps we do mention it, in order to publicize the miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a question. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides to the question. A rabbinic holiday might not be strong enough to require a change in ברכת המזון. On the other hand, the whole purpose of חנוכה is פרסומי ניסא, and mentioning it might serve that goal.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the Sages

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְהַזְכִּיר שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן?
phrases.english: What is the law about mentioning Hanukkah in Grace after Meals?
Since it is only by rabbinic law, we do not mention it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא מִשּׁוּם פַּרְסוֹמֵי נִיסָּא — מַדְכְּרִינַן?!
phrases.english: or perhaps, because of publicizing the miracle, we do mention it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַזְכִּיר שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to חנוכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חנוכה must be mentioned in ברכת המזון

steps.title: רב הונא: not required, but if mentioned, it goes in הודאה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that one does not have to mention חנוכה. Someone who wants to mention it does so in the הודאה blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה, in the name of רב הונא: one does not mention it. If he wants to mention it, he mentions it in the thanksgiving blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: mentioning חנוכה in ברכת המזון is optional. If one does mention it, it belongs in the הודאה blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a middle position. Because the day is דרבנן, there is no obligation. Still, mentioning it is allowed, and the place is fixed in the blessing of thanks (נודה לך). The theme of חנוכה is thanking God for the miracle, so it fits there.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not (need to) mention it
The thanksgiving blessing (נודה לך in ברכת המזון)

steps.confusionAlert: "אינו מזכיר" here means there is no obligation, not a prohibition. Today the universal custom is to say על הנסים, and that custom grows out of the "ואם בא להזכיר" option.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Sechora said that Rav Huna said:
One does not mention it.
And if he comes to mention it, he mentions it in the thanksgiving blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No obligation; whoever chooses to mention חנוכה does so in הודאה

steps.title: A guest wanted to mention חנוכה in בונה ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה visited רבא's house and planned to mention חנוכה in the בונה ירושלים blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה happened to come to רבא's house. He thought he would mention חנוכה in the blessing "Who builds Jerusalem."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about a guest who planned to put חנוכה in the wrong blessing. It is setting up רב ששת's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר יהודה probably saw בונה ירושלים as the general place for special additions, since ראש חודש and יום טוב (יעלה ויבוא) are added there. That assumption is about to be corrected.

keyTerms.meaning: The third blessing of ברכת המזון

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא.
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda happened by Rava's house.
He thought to mention Hanukkah in "Who builds Jerusalem."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical story testing where חנוכה belongs in ברכת המזון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An initial assumption that חנוכה goes in בונה ירושלים

steps.title: רב ששת: like תפילה, חנוכה goes in הודאה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת corrects the guest. Just as in תפילה (שמונה עשרה) חנוכה is mentioned in הודאה, so too in ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: it is like תפילה. Just as in תפילה it goes in the thanksgiving blessing, so too in ברכת המזון it goes in the thanksgiving blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת rejects the plan to use בונה ירושלים. He compares ברכת המזון to שמונה עשרה, where על הנסים is said in מודים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a direct comparison: תפילה already shows where חנוכה belongs. This confirms רב הונא's ruling about הודאה from Step 3 and rules out בונה ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: חנוכה, when mentioned in ברכת המזון, goes in נודה לך (הודאה), just as על הנסים goes in מודים in שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: Like prayer.
Just as in prayer it is in the thanksgiving blessing,
so too in Grace after Meals it is in the thanksgiving blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the guest's plan in Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea of mentioning חנוכה in בונה ירושלים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the model of תפילה, where חנוכה is placed in הודאה

steps.title: Must ראש חודש be mentioned in ברכת המזון?
steps.stepSummary: Building on the חנוכה question, the גמרא asks about ראש חודש. It is דאורייתא, which suggests it should be mentioned. But work is permitted on it, which suggests it need not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what about mentioning ראש חודש in ברכת המזון? Even if you say חנוכה, being rabbinic, does not require it, ראש חודש is from the Torah, so maybe it does. Or perhaps, since work is not forbidden on it, we do not mention it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new, related question about ראש חודש. It is setting up a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weakness of חנוכה was that it is only rabbinic, and ראש חודש does not have that weakness. But a different factor might matter: days that require mention, like שבת and יום טוב, forbid מלאכה, and ראש חודש does not.

keyTerms.meaning: If you conclude that... (a building-block question)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְהַזְכִּיר רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן?
phrases.english: What is the law about mentioning the New Moon in Grace after Meals?
If you say
that Hanukkah, which is rabbinic, does not require it,
the New Moon, which is from the Torah, does require it.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֲסִיר בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה —
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since performing labor is not forbidden on it,
we do not mention it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַזְכִּיר רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the חנוכה question to ראש חודש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ראש חודש, which is דאורייתא but permits work, must be mentioned in ברכת המזון

steps.title: רב and רבי חנינא disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב says one mentions ראש חודש. רבי חנינא says one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: one mentions it. רבי חנינא said: one does not mention it.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered with a dispute between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב follows the first side of the question: the Torah-level status of the day requires mention. רבי חנינא follows the second side: a day without a ban on מלאכה is not important enough for ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: Rav said: One mentions it.
Rabbi Chanina said: One does not mention it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposing answers to the question in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: mention ראש חודש; רבי חנינא: do not
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מחלוקת: רב says ראש חודש is mentioned in ברכת המזון; רבי חנינא says it is not.

steps.title: רב זריקא rules like רב, based on רבי אושעיא's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב זריקא says to follow רב, because רבי אושעיא's ברייתא agrees with him. Days with a קרבן מוסף, like ראש חודש and חול המועד, are mentioned in תפילה (in רצה, with repetition if left out) and in ברכת המזון, but they have no קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זריקא said: hold on to רב's view, since רבי אושעיא stands with him. For רבי אושעיא taught: on days with a מוסף offering, like ראש חודש and חול המועד, at מעריב, שחרית and מנחה one prays שמונה עשרה and adds something about the day in the עבודה blessing. If he did not say it, he must go back. There is no קידוש over a cup on these days, but there is a mention in ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the dispute in favor of רב by quoting a ברייתא that explicitly says ראש חודש is mentioned in ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the קרבן מוסף, not the ban on work, as the deciding factor. That undercuts רבי חנינא's reasoning. Its last line, "יש בהן הזכרה בברכת המזון," is the direct proof for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of a Festival
Something about the day's event (יעלה ויבוא)
The רצה blessing about Temple service
קידוש over a cup of wine

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows רב: ראש חודש is mentioned in ברכת המזון, because it is a day with a קרבן מוסף.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules in the ברייתא. Forgetting the mention in תפילה requires going back, but ברכת המזון has its own rules, so do not assume the "go back" rule here carries over to ברכת המזון.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זְרִיקָא: נְקוֹט דְּרַב בִּידָךְ,
phrases.english: Rav Zerika said: Take Rav's view in your hand,
since Rabbi Oshaya holds like him.
For Rabbi Oshaya taught:
Days on which there is an additional offering,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ וְחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד —
phrases.english: such as the New Moon and the intermediate Festival days,

phrases.aramaic: עַרְבִית וְשַׁחֲרִית וּמִנְחָה מִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה
phrases.english: at evening, morning and afternoon prayers one prays the eighteen blessings
and says something about the day's event in the Temple-service blessing.
And if he did not say it, we make him go back.
And there is no kiddush over the cup on them,
but there is mention of them in Grace after Meals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְרִיקָא: נְקוֹט דְּרַב בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in Step 7 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that ראש חודש is mentioned in ברכת המזון
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אושעיא's ברייתא: days with a קרבן מוסף have mention in ברכת המזון

steps.title: The ברייתא turns to days without a קרבן מוסף
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a contrasting category: days with no מוסף, listed as Monday, Thursday, Monday, fast days and מעמדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Days on which there is no מוסף offering, such as Monday, Thursday and Monday, and fast days and מעמדות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts its second category. Its wording raises a puzzle that the גמרא is about to address.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This category is set against the first one to show what changes when there is no קרבן מוסף. The listing of plain Mondays and Thursdays as separate items looks odd and sets up the question that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Groups of Israelites who prayed and fasted while their מִשְׁמָר served in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Days on which there is no additional offering,
such as Monday, Thursday and Monday,
and fast days and ma'amadot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא, now with the opposite category.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second category: days without a קרבן מוסף

steps.title: Why would ordinary Mondays and Thursdays be listed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא interrupts the ברייתא to ask why plain Mondays and Thursdays appear here, since nothing special is said on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Monday and Thursday: what are they doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the ברייתא's wording: ordinary Mondays and Thursdays have no special prayer insert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes on to say something about the day is added in שומע תפילה. That makes no sense for a regular Monday or Thursday, so the list as read seems wrong.

phrases.english: Monday and Thursday, what is their purpose here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of Monday and Thursday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ordinary weekdays have no special insert, so listing them makes no sense

steps.title: It means the Monday-Thursday-Monday fasts and מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the phrase as "Monday, Thursday and Monday of fasts and מעמדות." These are special fast days, not ordinary weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means Monday, Thursday and Monday of fast days and of מעמדות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא: the days listed are the special fast days that fell on Monday, Thursday and Monday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Public fasts, for example for rain, were set in a Monday-Thursday-Monday series, and the people of the מעמדות also fasted on certain days. So the list describes fast days, which fully explains why something is added to the prayer.

phrases.english: Rather, Monday, Thursday and Monday
of fast days and ma'amadot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֵׁנִי וַחֲמִישִׁי וְשֵׁנִי שֶׁל תַּעֲנִיּוֹת וּמַעֲמָדוֹת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list named ordinary Mondays and Thursdays as separate items
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase describes the Monday-Thursday-Monday series of fasts and מעמדות

steps.title: Days without מוסף: mentioned in שומע תפילה, not in ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: On these fast days, the day is mentioned in שומע תפילה, and one does not go back if he forgot. There is no קידוש and no mention in ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: At מעריב, שחרית and מנחה one prays שמונה עשרה and adds something about the day in "Who hears prayer." If he did not say it, he does not go back. There is no קידוש over a cup and no mention in ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by stating the rules for days without a מוסף. The contrast with the first category completes the proof for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Days without a מוסף get a weaker treatment: a mention in שומע תפילה with no requirement to go back, and nothing in ברכת המזון. This contrast shows that the קרבן מוסף is what earns a mention in ברכת המזון, so ראש חודש, which has a מוסף, is mentioned, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing "Who hears prayer" in שמונה עשרה
We do not make him go back

steps.whatToRemember: The dividing line is the קרבן מוסף. Days with a מוסף (ראש חודש, חול המועד) are mentioned in ברכת המזון; fast days without one are not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practice of saying יעלה ויבוא in ברכת המזון on ראש חודש and חול המועד, while saying nothing special in ברכת המזון on a public fast.

phrases.aramaic: עַרְבִית וְשַׁחֲרִית וּמִנְחָה מִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה,
phrases.english: At evening, morning and afternoon prayers one prays the eighteen blessings,
and says something about the day's event in "Who hears prayer,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא אָמַר — אֵין מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: and if he did not say it, we do not make him go back.
And there is no kiddush over the cup on them,
and there is no mention of them in Grace after Meals.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַרְבִית וְשַׁחֲרִית וּמִנְחָה מִתְפַּלֵּל שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה, וְאוֹמֵר מֵעֵין הַמְאוֹרָע בְּ״שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא after the clarification in Steps 10-11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A קרבן מוסף is what makes a day worth mentioning in ברכת המזון, which confirms רב's ruling for ראש חודש.

steps.title: Do we mention חנוכה in מוסף?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: is על הנסים said in מוסף on a day of חנוכה that also has a מוסף, such as שבת or ראש חודש?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the rule about mentioning חנוכה in the מוסף prayers? Do we say that since חנוכה has no מוסף of its own, we do not mention it there? Or perhaps the day itself is obligated in four prayers, so it is mentioned in all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. When שבת or ראש חודש falls during חנוכה, there is a מוסף, and we need to know whether על הנסים goes into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to see it. In the first, מוסף belongs only to שבת or ראש חודש and has nothing to do with חנוכה, so חנוכה is not mentioned. In the second, the whole day is a day of חנוכה, and every prayer said that day, all four of them, carries the mention.

keyTerms.meaning: To mention (here, to add על הנסים)
Four prayers: מעריב, שחרית, מוסף, מנחה

steps.confusionAlert: חנוכה itself never has a מוסף. The question only comes up on שבת חנוכה or ראש חודש טבת, when a מוסף is said because of the other day.

phrases.english: They asked:
What is the rule about mentioning Chanukah in the Musaf prayers?
Since it has no Musaf
of its own, we do not mention it?
Or perhaps it is a day
that is obligated in four prayers (so it is mentioned in all of them).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַזְכִּיר שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה בְּמוּסָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which days get a mention in תפילה to a new question about חנוכה in מוסף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is על הנסים said in a מוסף that belongs to שבת or ראש חודש?

steps.title: Two pairs of אמוראים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב יהודה say חנוכה is not mentioned in מוסף. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן say it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב יהודה both said: he does not mention it. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן both said: he mentions it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reporting a מחלוקת. Each side of the question has two אמוראים behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא and רב יהודה follow the first view: מוסף does not belong to חנוכה. רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן follow the second view: the day of חנוכה gets mentioned in every prayer said that day.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice we follow רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן: על הנסים is said in מוסף of שבת חנוכה and ראש חודש טבת.

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda
both said: he does not mention it.
Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan
both said: he mentions it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: אֵינוֹ מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 13 with a מחלוקת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a מחלוקת: one pair says no mention, the other pair says mention.

steps.title: אביי links the 'no mention' view to רב
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב הונא and רב יהודה are following רב. רב ruled that on שבת ראש חודש, the blessing after the הפטרה does not mention ראש חודש, because without שבת there would be no הפטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: the view of רב הונא and רב יהודה is the view of רב. For רב גידל said in the name of רב: when ראש חודש falls on שבת, the one who reads the הפטרה does not need to mention ראש חודש, because if it were not שבת there would be no הפטרה on ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries to show that the 'no mention' side has a source in an earlier ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule is that a day is not mentioned in something that is only there because of a different day. The הפטרה is there only because of שבת, so ראש חודש is left out of its blessing. In the same way, מוסף is there only because of שבת or ראש חודש, so חנוכה would be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who reads the הפטרה from the נביאים
For if it were not for

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה דְּרַב הוּא.
phrases.english: This view of Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda is Rav's view.
For Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
When Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbat,
the one who reads the Haftarah on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: does not need to mention Rosh Chodesh (in the blessing),
for if it were not Shabbat,
there would be no Haftarah on Rosh Chodesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא וְרַב יְהוּדָה דְּרַב הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds an earlier source for the 'no mention' side of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The view of רב הונא and רב יהודה that חנוכה is not mentioned in מוסף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that ראש חודש is not mentioned in the הפטרה blessing on שבת.

steps.title: The comparison does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the cases differ. ראש חודש never has a הפטרה at all, but חנוכה is mentioned in מעריב, שחרית and מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these the same? There, a הפטרה does not exist at all on ראש חודש. Here, the mention of חנוכה exists in מעריב, שחרית and מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects אביי's comparison and shows how the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הפטרה is completely foreign to ראש חודש, so it makes sense to leave ראש חודש out of its blessing. Mentioning חנוכה is already a normal part of that day's prayers, so adding it in מוסף is not foreign. That means רב's ruling does not prove the 'no mention' view.

phrases.english: Are these comparable?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם נָבִיא בִּדְרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ לֵיכָּא כְּלָל,
phrases.english: There, a Haftarah does not exist on Rosh Chodesh at all,
here, it (the mention of Chanukah) exists in Maariv, Shacharit and Mincha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the link to רב's ראש חודש ruling. It does not reject the 'no mention' view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A הפטרה never exists on ראש חודש, but the mention of חנוכה does exist in its other prayers.

steps.title: A better comparison: הפטרה at מנחה on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a closer case from רב. On a יום טוב that falls on שבת, the מנחה הפטרה blessing does not mention יום טוב, even though יום טוב does have a הפטרה in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like this: רב אחדבוי said in the name of רב מתנה, who said in the name of רב: when יום טוב falls on שבת, the one who reads a הפטרה at מנחה on שבת does not need to mention יום טוב, because if it were not שבת there would be no הפטרה at מנחה on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting אביי's case, the גמרא brings a different ruling of רב that really does match the חנוכה question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום טוב has a הפטרה in the morning, just as חנוכה is mentioned in other prayers. Still, the מנחה הפטרה exists only because of שבת, so יום טוב is left out. In the same way, רב would leave חנוכה out of מוסף, so the 'no mention' view does follow רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is comparable to this

steps.confusionAlert: Today there is no הפטרה at שבת מנחה. In רב's time some places read one, which is why this case exists.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule: a day is not mentioned in something that exists only because of another day, even if that day has its own mention elsewhere. That is the basis of רב הונא and רב יהודה, who say חנוכה is not mentioned in מוסף.

phrases.english: Rather, it is comparable to this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַחַדְבוּי אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: For Rav Achadvoi said in the name of Rav Mattana, who said in the name of Rav:
When a Yom Tov falls on Shabbat,
the one who reads a Haftarah at Mincha on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַזְכִּיר שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: does not need to mention Yom Tov,
for if it were not Shabbat,
there would be no Haftarah at Mincha on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison from step 15 with one that avoids the problem raised in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That רב הונא and רב יהודה follow רב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that יום טוב is not mentioned in the מנחה הפטרה blessing on שבת.
